findings.claim: Question 3 is typed '3 marks — Explain (HT)'.
findings.truth: The question is about why temperature stays constant while water boils. Nothing in P6.1 or P6.2 is bold, so this is assessed at both tiers. The (HT) flag is removed.
findings.evidence: spec P6.1 and P6.2 assessable outcomes carry no bold statements in specs/ocr/physics-b-21c-J259-bold.md

findings.claim: Question 5: 0.50 kg of water, a 50 W heater for 4.0 minutes, 'a temperature rise of 11°C'; the mark scheme calculates c = 2180 J/kg°C, says the value is lower than accepted, and blames heat loss.
findings.truth: 12 000 J into 0.50 kg of water can raise it by at most 12000/(0.50 x 4200) = 5.7 degC, so an 11 degC rise is impossible. Worse, heat loss makes a measured specific heat capacity too HIGH, not too low, because the measured energy input is larger than the energy the water actually absorbs. The data are changed to a 5.0 degC rise, which gives c = 4800 J/kg°C - above the accepted 4200 - and heat loss then explains the error correctly.

findings.claim: Question 1 asks why water is used as an engine coolant 'despite its relatively high cost compared with other fluids'.
findings.truth: Water is one of the cheapest coolants there is. The false premise is removed; the mark scheme is unaffected.
findings.evidence: settled fact

findings.claim: Flashcard 8 reads 'What fills in the blank: Cloze: Density = _____ ÷ volume.'
findings.truth: Two question stems are glued together and the drafting artefact 'Cloze:' is showing. Reworded to a single 'What is the missing quantity' stem, matching the fix used elsewhere in this programme.

findings.claim: Three places say a force-extension graph 'curves upward' beyond the limit of proportionality.
findings.truth: The lesson plots force on the y-axis and extension on the x-axis. Past the limit of proportionality the extension grows faster than the force, so the line bends towards the extension axis. 'Curves upward' is the shape you get with the axes swapped.
findings.evidence: settled fact; the lesson itself states force (y-axis) against extension (x-axis)

findings.claim: Question 3 is typed '4 marks — Required Practical Method'.

findings.evidence: spec chapter P8, PAG table; P6.3.3b and P6.3.6b cite PAG2

findings.claim: The fourth mark on question 6 requires the student to name hysteresis ('different extension on loading and unloading').

findings.evidence: spec P6.3.4 and the P6.3 narrative on rubber bands; no mention of hysteresis anywhere in J259

findings.truth: The working trails off in an ellipsis, and as written '0.36 / 0.8 x 10^-3' evaluates to 4.5 x 10^-4, not 450. The stated final answer of 450 kPa was already correct; only the model working is rebuilt.

findings.claim: Chapter mapping and coverage gaps.
findings.truth: This unit is chapter P6 in full: L1 = P6.1 plus P6.2, L2 = P6.3, L3 = P6.4 plus the P6.2 gas work, L4 = P6.5. The universe content is P6.5, not P1. P6.4 and P6.5 are marked 'separate science only', which is right for this subject. Untaught outcomes in P6: P6.1.1b (how to determine the densities of solid and liquid objects from length, mass and volume measurements, PAG1) - density gets one sentence and no method; P6.2.2 (mass conservation through melting, freezing, evaporation, condensation and sublimation, that physical change differs from chemical change, and that the material recovers its properties if the change is reversed) - not taught at all, and sublimation never appears; P6.5.1 in part - artificial satellites are never mentioned. Everything else in P6.1 to P6.5 is covered. On the question carried forward from the previous unit: P4.3.8 to P4.3.10 (moments, levers, gears) and P4.3.14 (reaction times) are NOT taught here either, so they remain untaught across this subject.
findings.evidence: spec chapter P6 assessable learning outcomes; lesson content read in full

findings.claim: Equation recall status and paper claims.
findings.truth: No lesson makes a paper-allocation claim, and none is possible on this board: J259 has Breadth papers (01 Foundation / 03 Higher) and Depth papers (02 / 04), each 90 marks, 1 hour 45 minutes, 50 per cent, and both papers assess all chapters. No lesson states which equations must be recalled. For the record: P6.1.2 (density = mass/volume), P6.3.5 (F = k x) and P6.4.2 (p = F/A) are recall-and-apply; P6.1.5a, P6.1.6, P6.3.7, P6.4.5 and P6.4.8 are select-and-apply, so they are given. Only P6.4.8 (p = rho g h) is bold in that list. All four lessons use g = 10 N/kg, which is this board's stated value. No control characters, no LaTeX outside delimiters, no banned strings.
findings.evidence: spec section 2a and section 3a assessment overview; Appendix 5h; spec narrative 'The Earth's gravitational field strength is therefore 10 N/kg'

summary: Chapter P6 in full; no factual physics errors in the exposition, but one unphysical practice data set whose mark scheme also reversed the direction of the heat-loss error, a force-extension graph described as curving the wrong way in three places, and a higher-only wrapper that is wrong in both directions in all three tiered lessons - hiding both-tier content in L2 and L4, and leaving Foundation readers an empty box in L2 and L3. Absolute zero, the Kelvin scale and the post-main-sequence star life cycle are off-spec for this board and are labelled, not deleted.
